Use case: stylized-concept. Create a landscape 3:2 Minecraft builder reference sheet, crisp voxel style, plain light background, vanilla Minecraft blocks only, no characters or animals. Two views side by side: LEFT straight-on front elevation, orthographic; RIGHT front-right three-quarter view at exactly the same scale. Show the same house consistently. Skilled human builder quality, actual block-grid massing and depth, projecting trim and recessed framed openings, roofs with verges, eaves and ridges, stairs/slabs/fences/walls/trapdoors/lantern details. No smooth non-voxel curves. Small labels FRONT ELEVATION and THREE-QUARTER; name key materials using exact block ids.

Site: suburban McMansion viewed from a cul-de-sac street, within a 44-block-wide by 32-block-deep lot, 14 blocks tall to highest ridge, two storeys plus attic, lawn, driveway and rear deck. Tall white-trimmed front gable is the highest point over a two-storey portico: four white quartz columns on a shallow porch, black double front door, stepped fanlight arch, tall stepped arched window above, black-shuttered windows either side, brass-black carriage lanterns. West/left three-car garage wing projects toward street, three wide cream panelled carriage doors with glass panes at top and black strap hinges, gray stone-veneer piers, long concrete driveway, two gable dormers on low dark roof over bonus room. Right of portico a projecting turret bay with tall arched windows, stepped conical roof and slim finial. East wing steps back under hip roof; large gray stone chimney on front wall between shuttered windows. Street-side lower walls stone veneer; upper floors beige lap siding, white bands, cornices, sills and alternating corner quoins. All dark asphalt-like shingle roofs, jumble of hips/gables/dormers/cone. Manicured lawn, foundation azalea hedges with small flowers, young staked birch on right lawn, lamp posts beside two-block-wide stone walk and porch steps, kerb, sidewalk, asphalt street. Rear wooden deck with railing, steps, patio table, chairs and grill behind kitchen French doors; show only what is naturally visible in the right view, do not add extra views or cutaways. Interior planned behind facade: double-height foyer, sweeping dark-oak staircase, hanging chandelier, open kitchen island/family room with stone fireplace and big TV, formal dining, office, garage mudroom; upstairs primary suite/closet/bath, three bedrooms, garage bonus room. Do not expose rooms unnaturally.

roles.role: visible rear deck and furniture interpretations

changes: Generated with the built-in image_gen tool and saved unchanged as concept.png in the current directory.

Block ids for visible objects are visual interpretations, not recoverable block metadata. The roles retain every planned block; inclusion does not mean that every planned block is visible. Small rear furniture and grill details are especially ambiguous.
The image adds reddish brick chimney caps, interpreted as bricks and brick_slab, outside the supplied palette.
The large roof behind the portico rises above the entry gable; the entry gable is not the tallest point.
The portico reads as two broad front column assemblies with paired detailing, rather than four clearly separated columns.
The entrance and shutters are brown dark oak rather than black.
Garage doors have custom panel geometry, small handles and strap hinges that do not exactly match vanilla birch_trapdoor, iron_bars or stone_button geometry.

The upper portico window has fine curved fanlight tracery; other windows, cornices, column mouldings, lantern brackets and tree stakes also include details smaller or smoother than vanilla block shapes permit.
The front gable contains an additional small attic window.
The garage projects only modestly ahead of the main facade, and its driveway appears shorter than the requested long driveway.
The left view shows visible roof and paving surfaces and slight perspective; it is not a strictly orthographic front elevation.
The two views do not establish an exact shared scale or a verifiable 44-by-32 lot and 14-block height. They also vary slightly in roof massing and front landscaping.
The walkway appears wider than two blocks in places, and its exact block width cannot be established.
The birch is relatively large and leafy for a young tree; its supports resemble thin diagonal timber stakes.
Additional low hedges border the lawn and east lot edge, beyond the requested foundation shrubs.
The rear deck, railing, steps, pale patio furniture and black grill are visible in the right view, but their exact block construction and the kitchen French doors are not clearly readable.
The interior rooms, staircase, chandelier, kitchen island, fireplace, TV, bedroom furniture and bathroom fixtures are hidden and cannot be confirmed from this exterior sheet.
The street suggests a curved kerb but does not show a complete cul-de-sac.
The material swatches name selected blocks only; they are stylized illustrations rather than exact vanilla block texture samples.
